messages.subject: [statnet_help] GWESP & GWNSP
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I'm testing if specific triad types in undirected networks are more/less
common than expected by chance. I've encountered some problems using the
triadcensus term, and thinking about using GWESP to model fully connected
triads and GWNSP for triads with two edges out of three (i.e. triad types
3+2). Can anyone recommend tips for using these terms, and are there
equivalent terms to model type 0 and 1 triads (i.e., triads with zero or one
edge)?

Thank you,

Amiyaal Ilany

messages.subject: [statnet_help] Interpretation of GWDegree
messages.body_plain:
Dear everyone,

We have run some models with the geometrically weighted degree term
(the model and results attached).

Is it correct to explain the positive effect of GWDegree as an
indicator of anti-preferential attachment (as in Hunter 2007) or
less-hub structures since the Equation 13 in Hunter 2007 suggested
that Alternating-k-star = exp(theta)( 2x Edges - GWDegree)?

The reason we have this question is that some papers  interpreted it
the same as Alternating-k-star such as in
http://www.projectguia.org/documents/research/100813/14_parra_jpah_2009_0295.pdf:
"(with a positive GWDegree) there was a strong tendency for
organizations with high degree (GWDegree) to collaborate with other
organizations that also have high degree."

Your comments will be appreciated a lot.
Best,

Yun Huang

m1<-ergm(co_prop ~ edges + gwdegree(0.69, fixed=T) + gwesp(0.9,fixed=T))

Monte Carlo MLE Results:
                         Estimate Std. Error MCMC s.e. p-value
edges                -13.15707    0.41581     0.098  <1e-04 ***
gwdegree            4.73408    0.33972     0.081  <1e-04 ***
gwesp.fixed.0.9   3.72574    0.05527     0.001  <1e-04 ***


-- 
Yun Huang
Science of Networks in Communities (SONIC)
Industrial Engineering and Management Sciences
Northwestern University
Google Voice: 847-220-7310
Office: FSB 1.459

messages.subject: [statnet_help] Algorithm for building an adjacency array from large (~6000x6000) adjacency matrix
messages.subject_clean: [statnet_help] Algorithm for building an adjacency array from large (~6000x6000) adjacency matrix
messages.body_plain:
Hello everyone,
First time posting. I'm hoping someone can help me through a data issue. I have a large adjacency matrix of production networks. The column represents a unit process (say, Steel milling). The rows indicate prior processes and raw material inputs. So column A might have connections to B and C (listed as rows). Step to Column B and it might have connections to A1 and B1 (these are raw resources listed as rows). Since column A connects to B, the network should also connect to A1 and B1. As I proceed through the columns, each column should end up being a network consisting of all the unit production processes and the raw material inputs. I then want to analyze each production network for certain network metrics and shapes.

I read in the matrix as a directed network. I wrote code that used the reachability function of sna to find all nodes there were reachable from each column node. I then built an adjacency array of all the different networks by zeroing out non reachable nodes in the original matrix and adding it to the adjacency array. Everything worked great on test data.

I tested it on the full matrix and it has been running for 36 hours. It appears that my computer with 12GB of ram is struggling and it's using hard disk writes to virtual memory severely slowing things down. Any suggestions on how to better optimize the reachability calculation or an alternate way to pull these network subsets out of the main adjacency network?

I have copied my code below. Thanks in advance for any advice.

X<- read.csv(file="SampNet2.csv",head=TRUE,sep=",",row.names=2)
labels<-X[1]
SampNet= as.matrix(X[2:8])
#Transpose matrix to reverse edge direction
tSampNet<-t(SampNet)

#plot network to verify
gplot(tSampNet,gmode='digraph',diag=T, usearrows=T, displaylabels=T, label.cex=.5)

#create a reachability matrix
Reach<-reachability(tSampNet)

#Function to extract subnetworks using reachability matrix. 
#each row of the reachability matrix represents a network. Function iterates
#through each row setting non-reachable nodes to zero
#Returns an array of size n equal to the number of columns in the original matrix
#each entry in the array is an adjacency matrix of the subnetwork

ExtNet<-function(x,y) 
{
	n<-nrow(x)
	out<-array(,dim=c(n,n,n))
	for (i in 1:n)
	{
		z<-y
		for(j in 1:n)
		{
			z[,j]<-x[i,j]*z[,j]
			z[j,]<-x[i,j]*z[j,]
		}
	z[is.na(z)] <- 0
	out[,,i]<-z	
	}
	return(out)
}

#Function loses labels for each matrix. NetArray is instantiated. Then must re-add labels 
#to array to preserve
NetArray<-ExtNet(Reach,tSampNet)
